items.formation: V dictionary/ない + ことにする
items.usage: Use for a speaker’s own deliberate decision or rule.
items.register: neutral; polite ending may be added
items.nuance: The subject chooses the action; ことになる presents an external decision.

examples.jp: 毎朝三十分歩くことにした。
examples.reading: まいあささんじゅっぷんあるくことにした。
examples.romaji: Maiasa sanjup-pun aruku koto ni shita.
examples.en: I decided to walk for thirty minutes every morning.

examples.jp: 甘い物は週末だけ食べることにします。
examples.reading: あまいものはしゅうまつだけたべることにします。
examples.romaji: Amai mono wa shūmatsu dake taberu koto ni shimasu.
examples.en: I’ll make it a rule to eat sweets only on weekends.

examples.jp: 今日は早く寝ることにしよう。
examples.reading: きょうははやくねることにしよう。
examples.romaji: Kyō wa hayaku neru koto ni shiyō.
examples.en: Let’s decide to go to bed early today.

items.meaning: it is decided that; come to be
items.formation: V dictionary/ない + ことになる
items.usage: Use when a rule, arrangement, or circumstance determines the outcome.
items.register: neutral; polite ending may be added
items.nuance: The decision is external or presented as a settled arrangement.

examples.jp: 会議は午後二時に始まることになっています。
examples.reading: かいぎはごごにじにはじまることになっています。
examples.romaji: Kaigi wa gogo ni-ji ni hajimaru koto ni natte imasu.
examples.en: The meeting is scheduled to start at two p.m.

examples.en: It was decided that the game would be canceled if it rained.

items.formation: V dictionary/ない + ことになっている
items.usage: Use for established schedules, rules, or conventions.
items.register: neutral; polite ending may be added
items.nuance: Often describes a standing rule rather than a one-time decision.

examples.en: This library has a rule against bringing in drinks.

examples.jp: 研修は金曜日に終わることになっています。
examples.reading: けんしゅうはきんようびにおわることになっています。

examples.en: The training is scheduled to finish Friday.

examples.jp: 入国したら、二週間以内に住所を届けることになっている。

examples.romaji: Nyūkoku shitara, ni-shūkan inai ni jūsho o todokeru koto ni natte iru.
examples.en: After entering the country, one is required to report an address within two weeks.

items.meaning: make an effort to; make sure to
items.formation: V dictionary/ない + ようにする
items.usage: Use for a conscious effort to establish or avoid a behavior.
items.register: neutral; polite ending may be added
items.nuance: Focuses on maintaining a practice; ようになる describes the resulting change.

examples.en: Let’s make sure not to look at our phones at night.

items.formation: V dictionary/ない + ようになる
items.usage: Use for a gradual change in ability, habit, or state.
items.register: neutral; polite ending may be added

examples.reading: はるになると、ひがながくなるようになります。
examples.romaji: Haru ni naru to, hi ga nagaku naru yō ni narimasu.

examples.jp: 毎日練習して、速く読めるようになった。

items.formation: V dictionary / Vない + つもりだ
items.usage: State a plan you currently intend to carry out.
items.nuance: An intention is not a confirmed external arrangement. Vないつもり means intending not to do; Vつもりはない denies an intention.
items.mistake: Do not use Vます before つもり.
items.comparison: ことにする focuses on deciding; つもり describes the resulting intention.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings in polite conversation

examples.jp: 夏休みに日本へ行くつもりです。
examples.reading: なつやすみににほんへいくつもりです。
examples.romaji: Natsuyasumi ni Nihon e iku tsumori desu.
examples.en: I intend to go to Japan during the summer vacation.

examples.jp: 今日はお酒を飲まないつもりだ。
examples.reading: きょうはおさけをのまないつもりだ。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa osake o nomanai tsumori da.
examples.en: I intend not to drink alcohol today.

examples.jp: 急いで決めるつもりはありません。
examples.reading: いそいできめるつもりはありません。
examples.romaji: Isoide kimeru tsumori wa arimasen.
examples.en: I have no intention of deciding in a hurry.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of つもりだ: 夏休みに日本へ行くつもりです。
question.answer: I intend to go to Japan during the summer vacation.
question.explanation: intend to; intend not to An intention is not a confirmed external arrangement. Vないつもり means intending not to do; Vつもりはない denies an intention.

items.formation: V dictionary/た + ついでに; N の + ついでに
items.usage: Use when adding a secondary action to a main errand.

items.formation: V dictionary/ N の + たびに
items.usage: Use for a repeated result that occurs each time an event happens.
items.register: neutral; polite ending may be added

items.formation: N + ごとに; V dictionary + ごとに

items.mistake: Use the て-form, including irregular forms: してはいけない and 来てはいけない.
items.comparison: Compared with ないでください, it sounds more like a rule or prohibition than a polite request.

items.meaning: may; it is all right to
items.formation: Vて + もいい; N + でもいい
items.usage: Use to grant or ask for permission.

items.comparison: Compared with なくてもいい, it permits doing something; なくてもいい permits omitting it.

examples.jp: 疲れたら、先に帰ってもいいよ。

examples.jp: 窓を開けてもいいですか。

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of てもいい: ここに名前を書いてもいいですか。
question.answer: May I write my name here?
question.explanation: may; it is all right to The focus is permission, not ability or obligation.

items.meaning: it is all right to; do not mind if
items.formation: Vて + もかまわない; い-adjくて / N・な-adjで + もかまわない
items.usage: Grant permission or state that a condition is acceptable.
items.nuance: The speaker says it causes no objection, rather than actively recommends it.
items.mistake: Do not infer obligation: permission means the action is allowed, not required.
items.comparison: てもいい is a more everyday equivalent; てもかまわない may sound slightly more formal.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings in polite conversation

question.answer: Would it be all right if I sat here?
question.explanation: it is all right to; do not mind if The speaker says it causes no objection, rather than actively recommends it.

exercises.question: Explain the usage distinction between なければならない and なくてもいい.
exercises.answer: なければならない: must; have to. なくてもいい: need not; may not.
exercises.explanation: Compared with べきだ, it expresses a stronger necessity and less personal advice. Compared with なければならない, it marks the absence of obligation.

lessons.title: Ability and difficulty
lessons.overview: Master ability and difficulty in practical N3 contexts.

items.formation: V dictionary + ことができる
items.usage: Use to state ability or possibility in a relatively formal, explicit way.
items.register: neutral to formal; often used in notices and explanations
items.nuance: The construction nominalizes the action and focuses on whether it is possible.
items.mistake: Use dictionary form before ことができる, not the ます-stem: 読むことができる.
items.comparison: Compared with potential verbs, it is more explicit and often more formal: 予約できる is shorter.

examples.jp: この機械で写真を印刷することができます。
examples.reading: このきかいでしゃしんをいんさつすることができます。
examples.romaji: Kono kikai de shashin o insatsu suru koto ga dekimasu.

examples.jp: 私は漢字を少し読むことができる。

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of ことができる: この機械で写真を印刷することができます。
question.answer: You can print photographs with this machine.

items.formation: Vます-stem + にくい
items.usage: Use when an action is difficult because of its nature, form, or circumstances.
items.register: neutral; polite ending may be added
items.nuance: It describes difficulty, not the speaker’s refusal or lack of desire.
items.mistake: Attach to the ます-stem: 読みにくい, not 読むにくい.
items.comparison: Compared with づらい, にくい can sound more objective; づらい often includes the speaker’s psychological difficulty.

examples.jp: この説明は専門用語が多くて分かりにくい。
examples.reading: このせつめいはせんもんようごがおおくてわかりにくい。
examples.romaji: Kono setsumei wa senmon yōgo ga ōkute wakari nikui.

examples.jp: 小さい文字は読み肉いので、拡大してください。

examples.romaji: Chiisai moji wa yomi nikui node, kakudai shite kudasai.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of にくい: この説明は専門用語が多くて分かりにくい。
question.answer: This explanation is hard to understand because it has many technical terms.
question.explanation: difficult to; hard to It describes difficulty, not the speaker’s refusal or lack of desire.

items.formation: Vます-stem + やすい
items.usage: Use when an action is easy to perform or a thing tends to produce a result.
items.register: neutral; polite ending may be added
items.nuance: It may describe physical ease or a tendency, depending on the verb.
items.mistake: Attach to the ます-stem: 使いやすい, not 使うやすい.
items.comparison: Compared with ことができる, it describes ease rather than mere possibility.

examples.jp: このアプリは操作しやすい。
examples.reading: このあぷりはそうさしやすい。
examples.romaji: Kono apuri wa sōsa shi yasui.

examples.jp: 駅から見つけやすい場所に看板を置いた。

examples.romaji: Eki kara mitsuke yasui basho ni kanban o oita.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of やすい: このアプリは操作しやすい。
question.answer: This app is easy to operate.
question.explanation: easy to; apt to It may describe physical ease or a tendency, depending on the verb.

items.meaning: be unable or reluctant to; cannot easily
items.formation: Vます-stem + かねる
items.usage: Use in polite refusals when accepting a request would be difficult or inappropriate.

items.nuance: It softens a refusal by presenting inability or hesitation rather than blunt rejection.

items.comparison: Compared with できない, かねる is more indirect and formal, especially in customer service.

examples.romaji: Kisoku-jō, henkin ni wa ōji kanemasu.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of かねる: そのご提案には賛成しかねます。
question.answer: I am afraid I cannot agree to that proposal.
question.explanation: be unable or reluctant to; cannot easily It softens a refusal by presenting inability or hesitation rather than blunt rejection.

items.formation: V stem + ようがない; suru noun + のしようがない
items.usage: State that there is no available method or means.

items.comparison: できない simply says cannot; ようがない explains impossibility through absence of a method.

exercises.explanation: Compared with potential verbs, it is more explicit and often more formal: 予約できる is shorter. Compared with づらい, にくい can sound more objective; づらい often includes the speaker’s psychological difficulty.

lessons.title: Passive
lessons.overview: Master passive in practical N3 contexts.

items.formation: V passive: 五段 う段→あ段 + れる; 一段 る→られる; する→される; 来る→来られる
items.usage: Use when the affected person or thing is the topic, or when the agent is less important.
items.register: neutral; polite ending may be added
items.nuance: The passive can highlight an unwanted experience as well as a neutral event.
items.mistake: Do not confuse passive られる with potential られる; context and the subject identify the meaning.
items.comparison: Compared with an active sentence, passive voice puts the recipient of the action in topic position.

examples.jp: この小説は多くの人に読まれている。
examples.reading: このしょうせつはおおくのひとによまれている。
examples.romaji: Kono shōsetsu wa ōku no hito ni yomarete iru.

items.meaning: suffer an unwanted action; adversative passive

items.usage: Use when an event caused trouble or inconvenience to the subject, even if the subject was not the direct object.
items.register: neutral; common in personal complaints
items.nuance: The passive marks the subject’s affected viewpoint and often conveys annoyance or loss.
items.mistake: The subject is the person inconvenienced; do not make the direct object the topic automatically.
items.comparison: Compared with ordinary passive, it emphasizes the subject’s adverse experience rather than the action’s result.

items.formation: N によって + passive verb
items.usage: Use によって to identify the agent or creator in formal descriptions, especially with works, discoveries, and systems.
items.register: formal, written, academic or news style
items.nuance: It gives prominence to the agent or means in an objective statement.

question.answer: This painting was painted by a famous artist.
question.explanation: be done by; through (passive agent) It gives prominence to the agent or means in an objective statement.

items.formation: 五段: う段→え段 + る; 一段: る→られる; する→できる; 来る→来られる
items.usage: Use to state ability or whether an action is possible for a subject.
items.register: neutral; polite ending may be added

lessons.title: Causative
lessons.overview: Master causative in practical N3 contexts.

items.formation: 使役: 五段 う段→あ段 + せる; 一段 る→させる; する→させる; 来る→来させる
items.usage: Use when a person causes or permits another person to perform an action.
items.register: neutral; polite requests use させてください
items.nuance: Context determines whether the causer forces the action or allows it.
items.mistake: The person made to act takes を with transitive verbs and に with many intransitive verbs.
items.comparison: Compared with てもらう, causative presents the causer’s control over another person’s action.

examples.jp: 先生は学生に作文を書かせた。
examples.reading: せんせいはがくせいにさくぶんをかかせた。
examples.romaji: Sensei wa gakusei ni sakubun o kakaseta.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of 使役: 先生は学生に作文を書かせた。

question.explanation: make or let someone do Context determines whether the causer forces the action or allows it.

items.meaning: be made to; be forced to do
items.formation: 使役 passive: 五段 あ段 + せられる/される; 一段 させられる; する→させられる; 来る→来させられる
items.usage: Use when the subject was compelled to perform an action by someone else.
items.register: neutral; often conveys complaint
items.nuance: It combines another person’s control with the subject’s experience of being made to act.
items.mistake: Do not omit the causative part: 食べられた means was eaten/could eat, while 食べさせられた means was made to eat.
items.comparison: Compared with ordinary passive, it says the subject had to perform the action rather than merely receive it.

examples.jp: 私は上司に残業させられた。

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of 使役受身: 私は上司に残業させられた。
question.answer: My boss made me work overtime.
question.explanation: be made to; be forced to do It combines another person’s control with the subject’s experience of being made to act.

items.meaning: please let me; allow me to
items.formation: V causative て-form + ください
items.usage: Use to politely ask permission to perform an action oneself.
items.register: polite; direct but respectful request
items.nuance: The speaker asks the listener to permit the speaker’s own action.
items.mistake: Use the causative て-form: 説明させてください, not 説明してください when asking to explain oneself.
items.comparison: Compared with てもいいですか, it is a more direct request for the listener’s permission and often precedes an action.

examples.reading: わたしからじじょうをせつめいさせてください。

items.formation: Vて + あげる
items.usage: Use when the speaker or another subject performs a favor for a recipient.
items.register: neutral; avoid imposing it on a superior without context
items.nuance: The action benefits the recipient; あげる presents the giver’s viewpoint.
items.mistake: Do not use あげる when the recipient is the speaker or a speaker-side person; use くれる/もらう appropriately.
items.comparison: Compared with くれる, あげる views the transfer or favor from the giver’s side.

items.meaning: give to me or my in-group; do for me

lessons.title: Comparison and degree
lessons.overview: Master comparison and degree in practical N3 contexts.

items.formation: N / plain clause + より
items.usage: Name the standard that the main description exceeds or differs from.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: The thing before より is the comparison baseline.
items.mistake: AよりBのほうが高い says B is more expensive, not A.
items.comparison: ほど〜ない uses a negative predicate to say less ... than.

examples.jp: 今日は昨日より暖かいです。
examples.reading: きょうはきのうよりあたたかいです。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa kinou yori atatakai desu.
examples.en: Today is warmer than yesterday.

examples.jp: 車より電車のほうが速い。
examples.reading: くるまよりでんしゃのほうがはやい。
examples.romaji: Kuruma yori densha no hou ga hayai.
examples.en: The train is faster than the car.

examples.jp: 聞くより、実際に見るほうが分かりやすい。
examples.reading: きくより、じっさいにみるほうがわかりやすい。
examples.romaji: Kiku yori, jissai ni miru hou ga wakariyasui.
examples.en: It is easier to understand by actually seeing than by hearing about it.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of より: 今日は昨日より暖かいです。

items.formation: N / plain clause + ほど + negative predicate
items.usage: Say that something does not reach the comparison standard.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: The noun before ほど supplies the higher standard.
items.mistake: Do not omit the negative ending in the “not as” construction.
items.comparison: AよりB is an affirmative comparison; BはAほど〜ない gives the reverse relation.

items.formation: Vば + same V dictionary + ほど; い-adjければ + same い-adj + ほど; な-adjなら + same な-adjな + ほど

items.formation: V plain + 代わりに; N + の代わりに; い-adj + 代わりに; な-adj + な代わりに
items.usage: Show substitution or a compensating tradeoff.
items.nuance: Identify whether one actor/action replaces another or one advantage balances a disadvantage.
items.mistake: A noun needs の: 先生の代わりに.
items.comparison: 一方で simply contrasts aspects; 代わりに often suggests exchange or compensation.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings in polite conversation

examples.jp: 今日は兄の代わりに店を手伝います。
examples.reading: きょうはあにのかわりにみせをてつだいます。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa ani no kawari ni mise o tetsudaimasu.
examples.en: Today I will help at the shop in my older brother’s place.

examples.jp: 車で行く代わりに、電車で行きました。
examples.reading: くるまでいくかわりに、でんしゃでいきました。
examples.romaji: Kuruma de iku kawari ni, densha de ikimashita.
examples.en: Instead of going by car, I went by train.

examples.jp: 家賃が安い代わりに、駅から遠いです。
examples.reading: やちんがやすいかわりに、えきからとおいです。
examples.romaji: Yachin ga yasui kawari ni, eki kara tooi desu.
examples.en: The rent is cheap, but in exchange it is far from the station.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of 代わりに: 今日は兄の代わりに店を手伝います。
question.answer: Today I will help at the shop in my older brother’s place.
question.explanation: instead of; in exchange for Identify whether one actor/action replaces another or one advantage balances a disadvantage.

exercises.question: Translate naturally: 車より電車のほうが速い。
exercises.answer: The train is faster than the car.
exercises.explanation: The thing before より is the comparison baseline.

exercises.question: Express this in Japanese using ほど〜ない: The exam was not as difficult as I expected.
exercises.answer: 試験は思ったほど難しくなかった。
exercises.explanation: Other natural wording is acceptable if it preserves the relationship. N / plain clause + ほど + negative predicate

exercises.question: Explain the usage distinction between より and ほど〜ない.
exercises.answer: より: than; comparison standard. ほど〜ない: not as ... as.
exercises.explanation: ほど〜ない uses a negative predicate to say less ... than. AよりB is an affirmative comparison; BはAほど〜ない gives the reverse relation.

lessons.title: Limiting and emphasis
lessons.overview: Master limiting and emphasis in practical N3 contexts.

items.formation: N + さえ; particles may combine: にさえ, でさえ
items.usage: Pick an extreme example or, with a conditional, a minimum requirement.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: The core assertion is surprising even for the marked item.
items.mistake: Do not confuse “even a child” with “only children”; さえ is not だけ.
items.comparison: まで can also mean even, often highlighting an unexpected addition.

examples.jp: 自分の名前さえ書けなかった。
examples.reading: じぶんのなまえさえかけなかった。
examples.romaji: Jibun no namae sae kakenakatta.
examples.en: I could not even write my own name.

examples.jp: 忙しくて、昼ご飯を食べる時間さえない。
examples.reading: いそがしくて、ひるごはんをたべるじかんさえない。
examples.romaji: Isogashikute, hirugohan o taberu jikan sae nai.
examples.en: I am so busy that I do not even have time to eat lunch.

examples.jp: この道具は子どもでさえ使えます。
examples.reading: このどうぐはこどもでさえつかえます。
examples.romaji: Kono dougu wa kodomo de sae tsukaemasu.
examples.en: Even children can use this tool.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of さえ: 自分の名前さえ書けなかった。
question.answer: I could not even write my own name.
question.explanation: even; only if (with conditional) The core assertion is surprising even for the marked item.

items.formation: N/phrase + こそ; reason clause + からこそ
items.usage: Strongly focus the information the speaker considers decisive.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Often contrasts the highlighted item with other possibilities.
items.mistake: It does not normally mean only to the exclusion of everything else.
items.comparison: だけ restricts; こそ emphasizes.

examples.jp: 今こそ始めるときです。
examples.reading: いまこそはじめるときです。
examples.romaji: Ima koso hajimeru toki desu.
examples.en: Now is precisely the time to start.

examples.jp: こちらこそ、ありがとうございます。
examples.reading: こちらこそ、ありがとうございます。
examples.romaji: Kochira koso, arigatou gozaimasu.
examples.en: It is I who should thank you.

examples.jp: 失敗したからこそ、分かったことがあります。
examples.reading: しっぱいしたからこそ、わかったことがあります。
examples.romaji: Shippai shita kara koso, wakatta koto ga arimasu.
examples.en: There are things I understood precisely because I failed.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of こそ: 今こそ始めるときです。
question.answer: Now is precisely the time to start.
question.explanation: precisely; the very thing/person; emphasis Often contrasts the highlighted item with other possibilities.

items.formation: N/phrase + まで
items.usage: Extend a situation to a surprising additional participant or consequence.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Different from endpoint まで; context can identify either meaning.
items.mistake: Do not automatically translate it as until when it marks an unexpected person or object.
items.comparison: さえ often picks an extreme example; まで highlights how far the situation extends.

examples.jp: 先生まで間違えました。
examples.reading: せんせいまでまちがえました。
examples.romaji: Sensei made machigaemashita.
examples.en: Even the teacher made a mistake.

examples.jp: 財布だけでなく、鍵までなくした。
examples.reading: さいふだけでなく、かぎまでなくした。
examples.romaji: Saifu dake de naku, kagi made nakushita.
examples.en: I lost not only my wallet but even my keys.

examples.jp: 忙しくて、休日まで働いた。
examples.reading: いそがしくて、きゅうじつまではたらいた。
examples.romaji: Isogashikute, kyuujitsu made hataraita.
examples.en: I was so busy that I worked even on my day off.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of まで: 先生まで間違えました。
question.answer: Even the teacher made a mistake.
question.explanation: even; an unexpected further extent Different from endpoint まで; context can identify either meaning.

items.meaning: things like; such a thing as; surprised quotation
items.formation: N + なんか/なんて; plain clause + なんて
items.usage: Give casual examples, downplay something, or express emotion about a fact.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Tone can be dismissive; context and intonation matter.
items.mistake: Do not use dismissive なんか about something a listener values in formal interaction.
items.comparison: など is a more neutral/formal way to list examples.

examples.jp: お茶なんかどうですか。
examples.reading: おちゃなんかどうですか。
examples.romaji: Ocha nanka dou desu ka.
examples.en: How about something like tea?

examples.jp: 一人で全部作ったなんて、すごいです。
examples.reading: ひとりでぜんぶつくったなんて、すごいです。
examples.romaji: Hitori de zenbu tsukutta nante, sugoi desu.
examples.en: It is amazing that you made it all yourself.

examples.jp: 私なんかには難しすぎます。
examples.reading: わたしなんかにはむずかしすぎます。
examples.romaji: Watashi nanka ni wa muzukashisugimasu.
examples.en: It is too difficult for someone like me.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of なんか・なんて: お茶なんかどうですか。
question.answer: How about something like tea?
question.explanation: things like; such a thing as; surprised quotation Tone can be dismissive; context and intonation matter.

items.meaning: covered in; full of undesirable things
items.formation: N + だらけ; N + だらけの + N
items.usage: Describe many unwanted items, errors, or marks.
items.nuance: Often carries a negative evaluation; it does not mean a completely filled container in every context.
items.mistake: Do not use it automatically for pleasant abundance; 花がいっぱい is more neutral than 花だらけ.
items.comparison: いっぱい is neutral “full/many”; まみれ strongly suggests something smeared or covered in a substance.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings in polite conversation

examples.jp: 作文が間違いだらけでした。
examples.reading: さくぶんがまちがいだらけでした。
examples.romaji: Sakubun ga machigai darake deshita.
examples.en: My composition was full of mistakes.

examples.jp: 泥だらけの靴を洗った。
examples.reading: どろだらけのくつをあらった。
examples.romaji: Doro darake no kutsu o aratta.
examples.en: I washed the mud-covered shoes.

examples.jp: この部屋はほこりだらけです。
examples.reading: このへやはほこりだらけです。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa hokori darake desu.
examples.en: This room is covered in dust.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of だらけ: 作文が間違いだらけでした。
question.answer: My composition was full of mistakes.
question.explanation: covered in; full of undesirable things Often carries a negative evaluation; it does not mean a completely filled container in every context.

exercises.question: Translate naturally: 忙しくて、昼ご飯を食べる時間さえない。
exercises.answer: I am so busy that I do not even have time to eat lunch.
exercises.explanation: The core assertion is surprising even for the marked item.

exercises.question: Express this in Japanese using こそ: There are things I understood precisely because I failed.
exercises.answer: 失敗したからこそ、分かったことがあります。
exercises.explanation: Other natural wording is acceptable if it preserves the relationship. N/phrase + こそ; reason clause + からこそ

exercises.question: Explain the usage distinction between さえ and こそ.
exercises.answer: さえ: even; only if (with conditional). こそ: precisely; the very thing/person; emphasis.
exercises.explanation: まで can also mean even, often highlighting an unexpected addition. だけ restricts; こそ emphasizes.

lessons.title: Lists and examples
lessons.overview: Master lists and examples in practical N3 contexts.

items.meaning: things such as; or things like
items.formation: NとかNとか; plain clause + とか
items.usage: Give casual, non-exhaustive examples.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: The list does not necessarily name every possibility.
items.mistake: Keep examples grammatically parallel; do not interpret とか as an exhaustive and-only list.
items.comparison: や is a simple noun list; とか can also follow clauses.

examples.jp: 週末は掃除とか洗濯とかをします。
examples.reading: しゅうまつはそうじとかせんたくとかをします。
examples.romaji: Shuumatsu wa souji toka sentaku toka o shimasu.
examples.en: At weekends I do things like cleaning and laundry.

examples.jp: パンとか果物とかを買ってきて。
examples.reading: パンとかくだものとかをかってきて。
examples.romaji: Pan toka kudamono toka o katte kite.
examples.en: Please buy things like bread and fruit and bring them back.

examples.jp: 映画を見るとか、本を読むとかして休みます。
examples.reading: えいがをみるとか、ほんをよむとかしてやすみます。
examples.romaji: Eiga o miru toka, hon o yomu toka shite yasumimasu.
examples.en: I relax by doing things like watching films and reading books.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of とか〜とか: 週末は掃除とか洗濯とかをします。
question.answer: At weekends I do things like cleaning and laundry.
question.explanation: things such as; or things like The list does not necessarily name every possibility.

items.formation: Vた + り, Vた + り + する; adjectives can also alternate with たり
items.usage: List representative actions or alternating states.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Although built from the た-form, the final する determines tense.
items.mistake: Do not omit する at the end of an ordinary complete verb-list sentence.
items.comparison: とか can list noun/clause examples; たり uses the た-form and often a final する.

examples.jp: 休みの日は本を読んだり、散歩したりします。
examples.reading: やすみのひはほんをよんだり、さんぽしたりします。
examples.romaji: Yasumi no hi wa hon o yondari, sanpo shitari shimasu.
examples.en: On days off I do things like reading and taking walks.

examples.jp: 昨日は掃除をしたり、料理を作ったりした。
examples.reading: きのうはそうじをしたり、りょうりをつくったりした。
examples.romaji: Kinou wa souji o shitari, ryouri o tsukuttari shita.
examples.en: Yesterday I did things like cleaning and cooking.

examples.jp: 最近は暑かったり、寒かったりします。
examples.reading: さいきんはあつかったり、さむかったりします。
examples.romaji: Saikin wa atsukattari, samukattari shimasu.
examples.en: Recently it alternates between hot and cold.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of たり〜たり: 休みの日は本を読んだり、散歩したりします。
question.answer: On days off I do things like reading and taking walks.
question.explanation: do things such as Although built from the た-form, the final する determines tense.

items.formation: NやNなど; NなどのN
items.usage: Mark examples as non-exhaustive.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Common in written explanations and lists.
items.mistake: NなどのN needs の before the following noun.
items.comparison: なんか is more casual and can be dismissive.

examples.jp: 野菜や果物などを買いました。
examples.reading: やさいやくだものなどをかいました。
examples.romaji: Yasai ya kudamono nado o kaimashita.
examples.en: I bought things such as vegetables and fruit.

examples.jp: 住所などの個人情報を確認します。
examples.reading: じゅうしょなどのこじんじょうほうをかくにんします。
examples.romaji: Juusho nado no kojin jouhou o kakunin shimasu.
examples.en: We will check personal information such as your address.

examples.jp: 会場には学生などが集まっていました。
examples.reading: かいじょうにはがくせいなどがあつまっていました。
examples.romaji: Kaijou ni wa gakusei nado ga atsumatte imashita.
examples.en: Students and others had gathered at the venue.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of など: 野菜や果物などを買いました。
question.answer: I bought things such as vegetables and fruit.
question.explanation: and the like; such as Common in written explanations and lists.

items.formation: N + をはじめ; N + をはじめとする + N
items.usage: Name a representative prominent example before referring to the broader group.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: The named example is a starting representative, not necessarily first in time.
items.mistake: A following noun normally uses をはじめとする or をはじめとした.
items.comparison: など gives examples without necessarily singling out a prominent representative.

examples.jp: 東京をはじめ、多くの都市を訪れました。
examples.reading: とうきょうをはじめ、おおくのとしをおとずれました。
examples.romaji: Toukyou o hajime, ooku no toshi o otozuremashita.
examples.en: I visited many cities, including Tokyo.

examples.jp: 先生をはじめ、皆さんに感謝しています。
examples.reading: せんせいをはじめ、みなさんにかんしゃしています。
examples.romaji: Sensei o hajime, minasan ni kansha shite imasu.
examples.en: I am grateful to everyone, beginning with my teacher.

examples.jp: 米をはじめとする食品を輸出しています。
examples.reading: こめをはじめとするしょくひんをゆしゅつしています。
examples.romaji: Kome o hajime to suru shokuhin o yushutsu shite imasu.
examples.en: They export food products, notably rice.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of をはじめ: 東京をはじめ、多くの都市を訪れました。
question.answer: I visited many cities, including Tokyo.
question.explanation: starting with; including notably The named example is a starting representative, not necessarily first in time.

exercises.question: Translate naturally: パンとか果物とかを買ってきて。
exercises.answer: Please buy things like bread and fruit and bring them back.
exercises.explanation: The list does not necessarily name every possibility.

exercises.question: Express this in Japanese using たり〜たり: Recently it alternates between hot and cold.
exercises.answer: 最近は暑かったり、寒かったりします。
exercises.explanation: Other natural wording is acceptable if it preserves the relationship. Vた + り, Vた + り + する; adjectives can also alternate with たり

exercises.question: Explain the usage distinction between とか〜とか and たり〜たり.
exercises.answer: とか〜とか: things such as; or things like. たり〜たり: do things such as.
exercises.explanation: や is a simple noun list; とか can also follow clauses. とか can list noun/clause examples; たり uses the た-form and often a final する.

lessons.title: Topics and relation
lessons.overview: Master topics and relation in practical N3 contexts.

items.formation: N + に関して; N + に関する + N
items.usage: Introduce the subject of information, inquiry, or discussion.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Generally more formal than について.
items.mistake: Use に関する before a noun, not に関しての as the basic taught attributive form.
items.comparison: について is common conversationally; に関して suits reports and notices.

examples.jp: 日程に関して質問があります。
examples.reading: にっていにかんしてしつもんがあります。
examples.romaji: Nittei ni kanshite shitsumon ga arimasu.
examples.en: I have a question regarding the schedule.

examples.jp: この制度に関して説明します。
examples.reading: このせいどにかんしてせつめいします。
examples.romaji: Kono seido ni kanshite setsumei shimasu.
examples.en: I will explain this system.

examples.jp: 環境に関する本を読みました。
examples.reading: かんきょうにかんするほんをよみました。
examples.romaji: Kankyou ni kansuru hon o yomimashita.
examples.en: I read a book about the environment.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of に関して: 日程に関して質問があります。
question.answer: I have a question regarding the schedule.
question.explanation: regarding; concerning Generally more formal than について.

items.formation: N + に対して; V/い-adj plain + のに対して; N/な-adj + なのに対して
items.usage: Set two contrasting facts side by side.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Different from the target use in 人に対して丁寧だ; here two clauses or groups contrast.
items.mistake: A verb clause requires の before に対して in this contrasting construction.
items.comparison: 一方で similarly contrasts aspects without the same nominalizing attachment.

examples.jp: 兄は静かなのに対して、弟はよく話します。
examples.reading: あにはしずかなのにたいして、おとうとはよくはなします。
examples.romaji: Ani wa shizuka na no ni taishite, otouto wa yoku hanashimasu.
examples.en: My older brother is quiet, whereas my younger brother talks a lot.

examples.jp: 去年は赤字だったのに対して、今年は利益が出た。
examples.reading: きょねんはあかじだったのにたいして、ことしはりえきがでた。
examples.romaji: Kyonen wa akaji datta no ni taishite, kotoshi wa rieki ga deta.
examples.en: Last year there was a deficit, whereas this year there was a profit.

examples.jp: 平日に対して、休日は利用者が多い。
examples.reading: へいじつにたいして、きゅうじつはりようしゃがおおい。
examples.romaji: Heijitsu ni taishite, kyuujitsu wa riyousha ga ooi.
examples.en: Compared with weekdays, there are many users on holidays.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of に対して比較: 兄は静かなのに対して、弟はよく話します。
question.answer: My older brother is quiet, whereas my younger brother talks a lot.
question.explanation: whereas; in contrast to Different from the target use in 人に対して丁寧だ; here two clauses or groups contrast.

items.formation: N + にとって; N + にとっての + N
items.usage: State how something is judged by or relevant to a person/group.
items.nuance: Usually followed by evaluation: important, difficult, useful, necessary.
items.mistake: Do not use it merely to name a topic: 日本語について話す, not 日本語にとって話す.
items.comparison: について marks a topic; に対して marks a target or contrast; にとって marks a standpoint.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings in polite conversation

examples.jp: 私にとって、家族が一番大切です。
examples.reading: わたしにとって、かぞくがいちばんたいせつです。
examples.romaji: Watashi ni totte, kazoku ga ichiban taisetsu desu.
examples.en: For me, family is the most important thing.

examples.jp: この説明は初心者にとって難しい。
examples.reading: このせつめいはしょしんしゃにとってむずかしい。
examples.romaji: Kono setsumei wa shoshinsha ni totte muzukashii.
examples.en: This explanation is difficult for beginners.

examples.jp: これは町にとっての大きな問題です。
examples.reading: これはまちにとってのおおきなもんだいです。
examples.romaji: Kore wa machi ni totte no ookina mondai desu.
examples.en: This is a major problem for the town.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of にとって: 私にとって、家族が一番大切です。
question.answer: For me, family is the most important thing.
question.explanation: for; from the standpoint of Usually followed by evaluation: important, difficult, useful, necessary.

exercises.question: Translate naturally: この制度に関して説明します。
exercises.answer: I will explain this system.
exercises.explanation: Generally more formal than について.

exercises.question: Express this in Japanese using に対して比較: Compared with weekdays, there are many users on holidays.
exercises.answer: 平日に対して、休日は利用者が多い。
exercises.explanation: Other natural wording is acceptable if it preserves the relationship. N + に対して; V/い-adj plain + のに対して; N/な-adj + なのに対して

exercises.question: Explain the usage distinction between に関して and に対して比較.
exercises.answer: に関して: regarding; concerning. に対して比較: whereas; in contrast to.
exercises.explanation: について is common conversationally; に関して suits reports and notices. 一方で similarly contrasts aspects without the same nominalizing attachment.

lessons.title: Dependence and means
lessons.overview: Master dependence and means in practical N3 contexts.

items.meaning: depending on; by means of; because of
items.formation: N + によって; N + による + N
items.usage: Identify a variable factor, method, or cause; determine the sense from context.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: These meanings share a form but are not interchangeable in translation.
items.mistake: Do not interpret every によって as the agent of a passive verb.
items.comparison: によると specifically cites an information source; によって does not by itself mean according to a report.

examples.jp: 値段は季節によって変わります。
examples.reading: ねだんはきせつによってかわります。
examples.romaji: Nedan wa kisetsu ni yotte kawarimasu.
examples.en: Prices vary depending on the season.

examples.jp: 練習によって、発音がよくなった。
examples.reading: れんしゅうによって、はつおんがよくなった。
examples.romaji: Renshuu ni yotte, hatsuon ga yoku natta.
examples.en: My pronunciation improved through practice.

examples.jp: 大雨による被害が出ました。
examples.reading: おおあめによるひがいがでました。
examples.romaji: Ooame ni yoru higai ga demashita.
examples.en: There was damage caused by heavy rain.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of によって: 値段は季節によって変わります。
question.answer: Prices vary depending on the season.
question.explanation: depending on; by means of; because of These meanings share a form but are not interchangeable in translation.

items.formation: Information source N + によると; often followed by そうだ/ということだ
items.usage: Name where reported information comes from.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: It attributes rather than independently verifies the information.
items.mistake: Use a source such as a forecast, report, or person, not a mere cause.
items.comparison: によって can mean due to or depending on; によると is the reporting frame.

examples.jp: 天気予報によると、明日は晴れるそうです。
examples.reading: てんきよほうによると、あしたははれるそうです。
examples.romaji: Tenki yohou ni yoru to, ashita wa hareru sou desu.
examples.en: According to the forecast, it will be sunny tomorrow.

examples.jp: 案内によると、入場は無料です。
examples.reading: あんないによると、にゅうじょうはむりょうです。
examples.romaji: Annai ni yoru to, nyuujou wa muryou desu.
examples.en: According to the notice, admission is free.

examples.jp: 友達によると、駅前の店は安いらしい。
examples.reading: ともだちによると、えきまえのみせはやすいらしい。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ni yoru to, ekimae no mise wa yasui rashii.
examples.en: According to my friend, the shop near the station is apparently inexpensive.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of によると: 天気予報によると、明日は晴れるそうです。
question.answer: According to the forecast, it will be sunny tomorrow.

items.formation: N / V dictionary + に従って
items.usage: Describe parallel change or following a rule/instruction.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: With change, the second development accompanies the first.
items.mistake: Vます cannot attach directly; use dictionary form.
items.comparison: とおりに stresses matching a model; に従って can also describe a developing correlation.

examples.jp: 説明に従って、番号を押してください。
examples.reading: せつめいにしたがって、ばんごうをおしてください。
examples.romaji: Setsumei ni shitagatte, bangou o oshite kudasai.
examples.en: Please press the number according to the instructions.

examples.jp: 時間がたつに従って、不安が減りました。
examples.reading: じかんがたつにしたがって、ふあんがへりました。
examples.romaji: Jikan ga tatsu ni shitagatte, fuan ga herimashita.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of に従って: 説明に従って、番号を押してください。
question.answer: Please press the number according to the instructions.

items.pattern: とおりに / どおりに
items.formation: V dictionary/た + とおりに; Nの + とおりに; some N + どおりに
items.usage: Match instructions, expectations, or a model.
items.nuance: Common noun combinations include 予定どおり and 時間どおり.
items.mistake: Do not pronounce every form どおり: 言ったとおり uses と.
items.comparison: によると gives an information source; とおりに describes acting or occurring in agreement with a model.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings in polite conversation

examples.jp: 説明したとおりに、名前を書いてください。
examples.reading: せつめいしたとおりに、なまえをかいてください。
examples.romaji: Setsumei shita toori ni, namae o kaite kudasai.
examples.en: Please write your name as I explained.

examples.jp: 予定どおりに出発しました。
examples.reading: よていどおりにしゅっぱつしました。
examples.romaji: Yotei doori ni shuppatsu shimashita.
examples.en: We departed as scheduled.

examples.jp: 地図のとおりに歩いたのに、道に迷った。

examples.romaji: Chizu no toori ni aruita noni, michi ni mayotta.

question.answer: Please write your name as I explained.
question.explanation: as; in accordance with Common noun combinations include 予定どおり and 時間どおり.

exercises.question: Explain the usage distinction between によって and によると.
exercises.answer: によって: depending on; by means of; because of. によると: according to.
exercises.explanation: によると specifically cites an information source; によって does not by itself mean according to a report. によって can mean due to or depending on; によると is the reporting frame.

lessons.title: Actions and process
lessons.overview: Master actions and process in practical N3 contexts.

items.meaning: while doing; although in some established contrasts
items.formation: V stem + ながら for simultaneous actions
items.usage: Describe one person doing two actions at the same time.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: The action in the main clause is normally the focus.
items.mistake: For this simultaneous-action use, the actor should be the same in both clauses.
items.comparison: 間に can locate a separate person’s action inside another event’s duration.

examples.jp: 音楽を聞きながら料理をします。
examples.reading: おんがくをききながらりょうりをします。
examples.romaji: Ongaku o kikinagara ryouri o shimasu.
examples.en: I cook while listening to music.

examples.jp: 地図を見ながら歩きました。
examples.reading: ちずをみながらあるきました。
examples.romaji: Chizu o minagara arukimashita.
examples.en: I walked while looking at the map.

examples.romaji: Memo o torinagara setsumei o kiite imasu.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of ながら: 音楽を聞きながら料理をします。
question.answer: I cook while listening to music.
question.explanation: while doing; although in some established contrasts The action in the main clause is normally the focus.

items.formation: Vた / Vない + まま; Nの / な-adjな / い-adj + まま
items.usage: Describe preserving a state or doing another action without changing it.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Often points out that a needed change was not made.
items.mistake: Use 靴を履いたまま for keeping shoes on, not 履いてまま.
items.comparison: ながら describes simultaneous actions; まま describes a continuing state.

examples.jp: 電気をつけたまま寝てしまいました。
examples.reading: でんきをつけたままねてしまいました。
examples.romaji: Denki o tsuketa mama nete shimaimashita.

examples.en: Please do not enter with your shoes on.

examples.reading: なにもいわないままかえった。
examples.romaji: Nani mo iwanai mama kaetta.
examples.en: They went home without saying anything.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of まま: 電気をつけたまま寝てしまいました。
question.answer: I fell asleep with the light left on.
question.explanation: with a state unchanged Often points out that a needed change was not made.

items.meaning: finish completely; do to the limit
items.formation: V stem + きる; potential: きれる; negative potential: きれない
items.usage: Emphasize finishing all of an action or exhausting an amount.
items.nuance: Often the amount or effort is significant.
items.mistake: きれない means cannot finish all, not merely do not do it.
items.comparison: てしまう can stress completion/regret; きる foregrounds total completion.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings in polite conversation

examples.jp: 長い小説を一週間で読みきりました。
examples.reading: ながいしょうせつをいっしゅうかんでよみきりました。
examples.romaji: Nagai shousetsu o isshuukan de yomikirimashita.

examples.jp: 量が多くて、食べきれません。

examples.jp: 最後まで走りきった。
examples.reading: さいごまではしりきった。
examples.romaji: Saigo made hashirikitta.
examples.en: I ran all the way to the finish.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of きる: 長い小説を一週間で読みきりました。
question.answer: I finished the entire long novel in one week.
question.explanation: finish completely; do to the limit Often the amount or effort is significant.

items.formation: V stem + かける; V stem + かけの + N
items.usage: Describe an action begun but incomplete, or just about to begin.
items.nuance: The precise stage depends on the verb; 読みかけ usually means partially read.
items.mistake: Do not assume the action was completed.
items.comparison: たばかり follows a completed event; かけ highlights an unfinished state.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings in polite conversation

examples.jp: 読みかけの本を机に置いた。
examples.reading: よみかけのほんをつくえにおいた。
examples.romaji: Yomikake no hon o tsukue ni oita.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of かける / かけの: 読みかけの本を机に置いた。
question.answer: I put the book I had partly read on the desk.
question.explanation: start to; be partway through The precise stage depends on the verb; 読みかけ usually means partially read.

items.meaning: come to; develop toward now; go do and return
items.formation: Vて + くる
items.usage: Track change toward the present/viewpoint, or an action followed by returning.
items.nuance: Distinguish temporal development from literal motion by context.
items.mistake: The direction is toward the viewpoint; future continuation away from now usually uses ていく.
items.comparison: ていく projects change forward; てくる often traces it up to now.
items.register: neutral; N4 bridge with N3 discourse applications

examples.jp: 日本語のニュースが少し分かってきました。

examples.jp: だんだん寒くなってきた。

examples.romaji: Dandan samuku natte kita.

examples.jp: 飲み物を買ってきます。
examples.reading: のみものをかってきます。
examples.romaji: Nomimono o katte kimasu.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of てくる: 日本語のニュースが少し分かってきました。
question.answer: I have begun to understand Japanese news a little.
question.explanation: come to; develop toward now; go do and return Distinguish temporal development from literal motion by context.

items.meaning: continue on; develop from now; do and go
items.formation: Vて + いく
items.usage: Present change continuing forward or movement away from the viewpoint.
items.nuance: Often appears with これから, 今後, 続ける.
items.mistake: Do not use ていく for a change explicitly traced up to now without a forward/away viewpoint.
items.comparison: てくる moves toward now or the speaker; ていく extends onward.
items.register: neutral; N4 bridge with N3 discourse applications

lessons.title: Tendencies and emotions
lessons.overview: Master tendencies and emotions in practical N3 contexts.

items.formation: V stem / N + がち; がちなN / がちのN
items.usage: Describe a recurrent tendency, often undesirable.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: More about repeated occurrence than visual resemblance.
items.mistake: Attach to the stem: 忘れがち, not 忘れるがち.
items.comparison: 気味 suggests a slight current condition; がち suggests a recurring tendency.

examples.jp: 忙しいと、朝ご飯を抜きがちです。
examples.reading: いそがしいと、あさごはんをぬきがちです。
examples.romaji: Isogashii to, asagohan o nukigachi desu.
examples.en: When I am busy, I tend to skip breakfast.

examples.jp: 最近、授業を休みがちだ。
examples.reading: さいきん、じゅぎょうをやすみがちだ。
examples.romaji: Saikin, jugyou o yasumigachi da.
examples.en: Recently I have tended to miss class.

examples.jp: 彼は子どものころ病気がちでした。
examples.reading: かれはこどものころびょうきがちでした。
examples.romaji: Kare wa kodomo no koro byoukigachi deshita.
examples.en: He was often ill as a child.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of がち: 忙しいと、朝ご飯を抜きがちです。
question.answer: When I am busy, I tend to skip breakfast.
question.explanation: tend to; often fall into More about repeated occurrence than visual resemblance.

items.meaning: a little; showing a slight tendency
items.formation: V stem / N + 気味（ぎみ）
items.usage: Describe a mild condition, often unwanted and felt now or recently.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Common combinations: 疲れ気味, 風邪気味, 遅れ気味.
items.mistake: Do not attach to every adjective freely; learn common combinations.
items.comparison: がち describes repeated tendency; 気味 indicates a slight state.

examples.jp: 今日は少し疲れ気味です。
examples.reading: きょうはすこしつかれぎみです。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa sukoshi tsukaregimi desu.
examples.en: I am a little tired today.

examples.jp: 風邪気味なので、早く寝ます。
examples.reading: かぜぎみなので、はやくねます。
examples.romaji: Kazegimi na node, hayaku nemasu.

examples.romaji: Shigoto ga okuregimi ni natte imasu.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of 気味: 今日は少し疲れ気味です。
question.answer: I am a little tired today.
question.explanation: a little; showing a slight tendency Common combinations: 疲れ気味, 風邪気味, 遅れ気味.

items.meaning: -ish; prone to; having much of a quality
items.formation: Selected N / V stem / adjective stem + っぽい
items.usage: Describe a noticeable quality or tendency in an い-adjective-like form.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Common words include 子どもっぽい, 忘れっぽい, 油っぽい.
items.mistake: It conjugates like an い-adjective: 子どもっぽくない.
items.comparison: がち counts recurrence; っぽい presents a characteristic or impression.

examples.reading: このりょうりはあぶらっぽくありません。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri wa aburappoku arimasen.
examples.en: This dish is not greasy.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of っぽい: この服は少し子どもっぽい。
question.answer: These clothes look a little childish.
question.explanation: -ish; prone to; having much of a quality Common words include 子どもっぽい, 忘れっぽい, 油っぽい.

items.formation: V/い-adj plain / N / な-adj stem + に決まっている
items.usage: Express strong subjective certainty.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Can sound dismissive of doubts; the speaker’s certainty is not objective proof.
items.mistake: Do not add だ between a noun and に決まっている.
items.comparison: に違いない is also a strong deduction, often somewhat more measured.

examples.romaji: Konna jikan nara, mise wa shimatte iru ni kimatte imasu.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of に決まっている: そんな話はうそに決まっている。
question.answer: That story must be a lie.

items.meaning: show signs of feeling; show a desire to
items.formation: Selected emotion い-adj stem + がる; な-adj stem + がる; V stem + たがる
items.usage: Describe observable signs of another person’s feelings or wishes.
items.nuance: Often appears in ている to describe current visible behavior. Only certain emotion words combine naturally.
items.mistake: Do not freely add がる to every adjective; 楽しい → 楽しがる is possible, but factual size adjectives do not use it this way.
items.comparison: たい commonly expresses the speaker’s own desire; たがる reports another person’s displayed desire.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings in polite conversation

examples.romaji: Kodomo ga inu o kowagatte imasu.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of がる / たがる: 子どもが犬を怖がっています。
question.answer: The child is showing fear of the dog.
question.explanation: show signs of feeling; show a desire to Often appears in ている to describe current visible behavior. Only certain emotion words combine naturally.

items.formation: V/い-adj plain + ふりをする; な-adj + な; N + の

examples.romaji: Genki na furi o shinakute mo ii desu yo.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of ふりをする: 分からないふりをしました。

items.formation: Emotion/sensation Vて / い-adjくて / な-adjで + たまらない
items.usage: Express a feeling or physical sensation that is hard to contain.
items.nuance: Typically describes the speaker’s internal state; third-person descriptions need evidence or reporting.
items.mistake: It is not a general intensifier for every objective fact.
items.comparison: てしょうがない often overlaps; たまらない strongly stresses inability to bear the intensity.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings in polite conversation

lessons.title: Effort and attempt

items.formation: V volitional + とする
items.usage: Describe attempting an action or the moment just before it.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: The context determines attempt versus imminent action; success is not guaranteed.
items.mistake: This よう is part of the volitional, not dictionary form + よう.
items.comparison: てみる tries an action to see its result; ようとする focuses on attempting to start it.

examples.jp: ドアを開けようとしたが、開かなかった。

items.comparison: てみる is exploratory; てみせる demonstrates or resolves to prove.

examples.jp: 次の試験には必ず合格してみせる。

examples.jp: 先生が一度やってみせました。

examples.jp: この仕事を最後まで終わらせてみせます。

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of てみせる: 次の試験には必ず合格してみせる。

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of てみる: この料理を食べてみたいです。

lessons.title: Nominalization and truths
lessons.overview: Master nominalization and truths in practical N3 contexts.

items.formation: Plain verb/clause + こと; な-adjな / Nの where required
items.usage: Turn a clause into a noun-like concept.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Common in general rules, abstract facts, and fixed patterns like ことができる.
items.mistake: Do not treat こと and の as interchangeable inside fixed grammatical constructions.
items.comparison: の often suits directly perceived actions; こと often treats an abstract idea.

examples.jp: 毎日続けることが大切です。
examples.reading: まいにちつづけることがたいせつです。
examples.romaji: Mainichi tsuzukeru koto ga taisetsu desu.
examples.en: Continuing every day is important.

examples.jp: 日本語を学ぶことは楽しい。
examples.reading: にほんごをまなぶことはたのしい。
examples.romaji: Nihongo o manabu koto wa tanoshii.
examples.en: Learning Japanese is enjoyable.

examples.jp: 約束を守ることを忘れないでください。
examples.reading: やくそくをまもることをわすれないでください。
examples.romaji: Yakusoku o mamoru koto o wasurenaide kudasai.
examples.en: Please do not forget to keep your promise.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of こと: 毎日続けることが大切です。
question.answer: Continuing every day is important.
question.explanation: nominalize an action or fact Common in general rules, abstract facts, and fixed patterns like ことができる.

items.meaning: nominalize a concrete action; refer to one
items.formation: Plain clause + の; な-adjな / Nな for explanatory nominal clauses
items.usage: Treat an action as a noun or replace a recoverable noun.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Especially common for observing an action and in のが好き/のは難しい.
items.mistake: Before a perception verb, の is usually natural: 走っているのを見た.
items.comparison: こと commonly treats an abstract idea; の can refer to an observed event or “the one.”

examples.jp: 子どもが走っているのを見ました。
examples.reading: こどもがはしっているのをみました。
examples.romaji: Kodomo ga hashitte iru no o mimashita.
examples.en: I saw a child running.

examples.jp: 早く起きるのは難しいです。
examples.reading: はやくおきるのはむずかしいです。
examples.romaji: Hayaku okiru no wa muzukashii desu.
examples.en: Getting up early is difficult.

examples.jp: 赤いのをください。
examples.reading: あかいのをください。
examples.romaji: Akai no o kudasai.
examples.en: Please give me the red one.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of の: 子どもが走っているのを見ました。
question.answer: I saw a child running.
question.explanation: nominalize a concrete action; refer to one Especially common for observing an action and in のが好き/のは難しい.

items.meaning: the fact that; the meaning that
items.formation: Plain clause + ということ; N/な-adj + だということ
items.usage: Package the content of a statement as a fact or proposition.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: It makes the content being discussed explicit.
items.mistake: Retain the plain copula when quoting a noun predicate: 学生だということ.
items.comparison: こと directly nominalizes; ということ often foregrounds a stated content or conclusion.

examples.jp: 明日が休みだということを忘れていました。
examples.reading: あしたがやすみだということをわすれていました。
examples.romaji: Ashita ga yasumi da to iu koto o wasurete imashita.
examples.en: I had forgotten that tomorrow is a day off.

examples.jp: 彼が来ないということは、まだ聞いていません。
examples.reading: かれがこないということは、まだきいていません。
examples.romaji: Kare ga konai to iu koto wa, mada kiite imasen.
examples.en: I have not yet heard that he is not coming.

examples.jp: 全員が参加できるということが分かりました。

examples.romaji: Zenin ga sanka dekiru to iu koto ga wakarimashita.
examples.en: We found out that everyone can participate.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of ということ: 明日が休みだということを忘れていました。
question.answer: I had forgotten that tomorrow is a day off.
question.explanation: the fact that; the meaning that It makes the content being discussed explicit.

items.meaning: as for what is called; defines a term
items.formation: N/quoted phrase + というのは ... ことだ / 意味だ
items.usage: Explain a name, term, or concept.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Common when restating unfamiliar vocabulary for the reader.
items.mistake: Do not confuse explanatory というのは with a hearsay report.
items.comparison: ということ packages content; というのは makes that content or term the topic for explanation.

examples.jp: 定休日というのは、毎週決まって休む日のことです。
examples.reading: ていきゅうびというのは、まいしゅうきまってやすむひのことです。

examples.jp: この印というのは、何を表していますか。

examples.romaji: Kono shirushi to iu no wa, nani o arawashite imasu ka.
examples.en: What does this symbol represent?

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of というのは: 定休日というのは、毎週決まって休む日のことです。
question.answer: A regular closing day means the fixed day each week when a business is closed.
question.explanation: as for what is called; defines a term Common when restating unfamiliar vocabulary for the reader.

items.meaning: do ... but; it is true ... however
items.formation: Repeat the same plain predicate around ことは: VことはVが; い-adjことはい-adjが; な-adjなことはな-adjだが
items.usage: Concede a limited truth before adding a reservation.
items.nuance: The repetition emphasizes that the basic fact is accepted, but it may not meet expectations.
items.mistake: Do not confuse with Vことはない, which often means there is no need.
items.comparison: ものの directly links a fact and contrast; this pattern explicitly concedes the fact through repetition.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings in polite conversation

exercises.answer: こと: nominalize an action or fact. の: nominalize a concrete action; refer to one.

lessons.title: Connectors and discourse
lessons.overview: Master connectors and discourse in practical N3 contexts.

items.formation: Connector at the start of a restatement or conclusion
items.usage: Restate the previous content more directly or draw its summary implication.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: The following clause should clarify the previous point.
items.mistake: Do not use it merely to add an unrelated new fact.
items.comparison: そのため introduces a consequence; つまり reformulates meaning.

examples.jp: 今日は定休日です。つまり、店は開いていません。
examples.reading: きょうはていきゅうびです。つまり、みせはあいていません。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa teikyuubi desu. Tsumari, mise wa aite imasen.
examples.en: Today is the regular closing day. In other words, the shop is not open.

examples.jp: 一人千円です。つまり、二人で二千円になります。
examples.reading: ひとりせんえんです。つまり、ふたりでにせんえんになります。
examples.romaji: Hitori sen en desu. Tsumari, futari de nisen en ni narimasu.
examples.en: It is a thousand yen each. That means two thousand yen for two people.

examples.jp: 彼は父の兄です。つまり、私のおじです。
examples.reading: かれはちちのあにです。つまり、わたしのおじです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa chichi no ani desu. Tsumari, watashi no oji desu.
examples.en: He is my father’s older brother. In other words, he is my uncle.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of つまり: 今日は定休日です。つまり、店は開いていません。
question.answer: Today is the regular closing day. In other words, the shop is not open.
question.explanation: in other words; that is The following clause should clarify the previous point.

items.formation: Previous cause. そのため、result.
items.usage: Connect an already stated reason to its consequence.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: その points back to the preceding situation.
items.mistake: The following content must be a consequence, not simply a rewording.
items.comparison: その結果 emphasizes the outcome of an action/process; そのため can follow any causal situation.

examples.jp: 大雪が降りました。そのため、電車が止まりました。

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of そのため: 大雪が降りました。そのため、電車が止まりました。
question.answer: It snowed heavily. As a result, the trains stopped.
question.explanation: therefore; for that reason その points back to the preceding situation.

items.formation: Previous action/process. その結果、outcome.
items.usage: Identify what happened as the outcome of the preceding effort, process, or event.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Useful for reading the structure of reports.
items.mistake: The result need not be positive; the phrase itself does not mean success.
items.comparison: そのため highlights the causal reason; その結果 foregrounds the outcome.

examples.jp: 毎日練習した。その結果、発音がよくなった。

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of その結果: 毎日練習した。その結果、発音がよくなった。
question.answer: I practiced every day. As a result, my pronunciation improved.
question.explanation: as a result Useful for reading the structure of reports.

lessons.title: Advanced N3 bridge
lessons.overview: Master advanced n3 bridge in practical N3 contexts.

items.formation: Plain clause / N + というより
items.usage: Replace an initial description with a more accurate one.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: The second description is preferred as the better characterization.
items.mistake: Do not treat it as a numerical greater-than comparison.
items.comparison: より compares degree; というより compares ways of describing something.

examples.jp: 怒っているというより、心配しています。
examples.reading: おこっているというより、しんぱいしています。
examples.romaji: Okotte iru to iu yori, shinpai shite imasu.

items.nuance: Often an emphatic judgment rather than mathematical impossibility.
items.mistake: Do not confuse with わけではない, which may only partly deny a claim.

items.formation: V/い-adj plain + ものだから; な-adjな / Nな + ものだから

items.mistake: Present noun/な-adjective links commonly use な: 初めてなものだから.
items.comparison: ので gives a comparatively neutral reason; ものだから foregrounds the explanatory justification.

question.explanation: because; the reason is (explanation/excuse) Can sound apologetic or excuse-like; not a neutral technical cause in every setting.

items.formation: V/い-adj plain + ことから; な-adjな / Nである + ことから
items.usage: Use an observable fact as the basis for a conclusion, reason, or name.
items.register: neutral; use polite endings where appropriate
items.nuance: Common in explanatory writing, including how places get names.
items.mistake: The first clause should provide the factual basis, not merely a desired purpose.
items.comparison: ために can express purpose; ことから explains reasoning from a fact.

examples.jp: 形が星に似ていることから、この名前が付きました。
examples.reading: かたちがほしににていることから、このなまえがつきました。
examples.romaji: Katachi ga hoshi ni nite iru koto kara, kono namae ga tsukimashita.
examples.en: It got this name because its shape resembles a star.

examples.jp: 駅に近いことから、この場所を選びました。
examples.reading: えきにちかいことから、このばしょをえらびました。
examples.romaji: Eki ni chikai koto kara, kono basho o erabimashita.
examples.en: We chose this location because it is close to the station.

examples.jp: 電気がついていることから、誰かいると考えた。
examples.reading: でんきがついていることから、だれかいるとかんがえた。
examples.romaji: Denki ga tsuite iru koto kara, dareka iru to kangaeta.
examples.en: From the fact that the light was on, I thought someone was there.

question.question: Translate this sentence and explain the role of ことから: 形が星に似ていることから、この名前が付きました。
question.answer: It got this name because its shape resembles a star.
question.explanation: from the fact that; because (basis) Common in explanatory writing, including how places get names.

exercises.question: Translate naturally: 旅行というより、仕事でした。
exercises.answer: It was work rather than a trip.
exercises.explanation: The second description is preferred as the better characterization.

exercises.question: Express this in Japanese using わけがない: Since I have not heard the explanation, there is no way I would understand.
exercises.answer: 説明を聞いていないのだから、分かるわけがない。
exercises.explanation: Other natural wording is acceptable if it preserves the relationship. V/い-adj plain + わけがない; な-adjな / Nの + わけがない

exercises.question: Explain the usage distinction between というより and わけがない.
exercises.answer: というより: rather than saying; more accurately. わけがない: there is no way that.
exercises.explanation: より compares degree; というより compares ways of describing something. はずがない also expresses strong negative expectation; わけがない is often more emphatic.

confusions.explanation: ために states a purpose with an intentional action; ように often targets a desired state or ability.
confusions.example_a: 日本で働くために勉強する。
confusions.translation_a: I study in order to work in Japan.
confusions.example_b: 漢字が読めるように練習する。
confusions.translation_b: I practice so that I can read kanji.

confusions.explanation: 様態 is visual impression; 伝聞 reports information heard from someone.
confusions.translation_a: It looks like it will rain.
confusions.translation_b: I hear it will rain tomorrow.

confusions.explanation: はずだ is an expectation; わけだ is a conclusion that explains a situation.
confusions.example_b: 道が空いている。早く着いたわけだ。
confusions.translation_b: The road is clear. That explains why we arrived early.

confusions.explanation: のに marks an unexpected contrast; ても means even if/even though and often frames a condition.
confusions.example_a: 約束したのに来なかった。
confusions.translation_a: Although they promised, they did not come.
confusions.translation_b: Even if it rains, I will go.
